items.title: Clean install from the real registry, four package managers, three systems
items.proves: Names, scope, provenance and Yarn's one-day gate work on the real registry; no hidden toolchain dependency; the guide's commands work.
items.does_not_prove: A never-used operating system; a user's proxy or policy; Smart App Control; the Windows vsift.cmd shim from cmd.exe (L-109); that hosted images are clean machines (L-112).

producer.description: Hosted dispatch workflow with a version input: npm, pnpm, Yarn and Bun on Windows, macOS and Ubuntu, global and one-shot, scripts disabled, optional dependencies omitted, hostile file names and a fake ffmpeg on PATH through the launcher, npm audit signatures and gh attestation verify in the same job, in a scrubbed environment (cargo, rustc, git and python must not resolve).

evidence.note: The twelve clean-install jobs (npm, pnpm, Yarn and Bun on Windows, macOS and Ubuntu) of this run at 6aa5403: vsift-cli 0.1.0 installed from the real registry with cargo, rustc, rustup, git and python not resolving (asserted first); global (Yarn: project) and one-shot installs with scripts disabled; --version names 0.1.0 and the tag commit; hostile file names and arguments through the PowerShell, shell and Bun shims; a fake ffmpeg planted in the working directory and on PATH (SEC-02); optional dependencies omitted fail with exit 127; npm audit signatures and gh attestation verify. For 0.1.0 only. Yarn held 0.1.0 back for its first day and the documented exemption passed; the Windows vsift.cmd shim is an observation, not a pass (L-109, #257).

prior.note: The twelve-job npm matrix (Windows, macOS and Ubuntu by npm, pnpm, Yarn and Bun) from a local Verdaccio registry. The runners carry rustup and cargo on PATH, so this is not a clean machine, and the registry is not the real one.
The same matrix on the 0.1.0 tag's publish dispatch; still a local registry.

One install of 0.1.0 from the real registry, with npm only, on the maintainer's Windows 11 development machine (npm audit signatures 4 and 4, npx vsift --version). No pnpm, Yarn or Bun, no other system, not a clean machine.

items.title: Extracted native archive on each target
items.proves: install.md section 3 works end to end: download from the GitHub release, checksum, attestation, extract, run --version and setup check, skill byte-identical to the tag's, no Node.js on PATH.
items.does_not_prove: The prompts a browser download triggers.

producer.description: Hosted dispatch workflow, three jobs, one per target.

evidence.note: The three archive jobs of this run at 6aa5403: the three archives and SHA256SUMS downloaded from the v0.1.0 release, checksums and attestations verified, extracted, each executable in the right format, the system's own run with --version (0.1.0 and the tag commit) and setup check --json with no Node.js, Rust, Git or Python on PATH, and the shipped skill byte-identical to the tag's. For 0.1.0 only; no browser download (RQ-17).

items.title: Offline artifact-directory install with the real reviewed artifacts
items.proves: D-07's offline path with real bytes: components activated, setup check ready, a tampered file refused.
items.does_not_prove: A publisher's future file retention (L-099).

producer.description: Hosted Ubuntu 24.04 job: a download step, then a container with --network none that runs setup install with --artifact-dir.

evidence.note: The offline-install job of this run at 6aa5403: the three real reviewed artifacts downloaded by the published binary's own plan (size and SHA-256 checked) and installed with --artifact-dir in a container with --network none: all three components activated, setup check ready, a rerun already_current; the same install without the folder failed as offline; a changed byte was INTEGRITY_FAILURE (digest_mismatch), a missing file INVALID_ARGUMENT (artifact_missing), a relative folder INVALID_ARGUMENT. The minimal Ubuntu image was given libgomp1, which the whisper.cpp build needs (L-110, #256). For 0.1.0 only.

prior.note: The offline path has run with stand-in artifacts only; the managed smoke downloads the real files online, from a source-built binary.

items.title: Upgrade from 0.1.0, 0.1.0 JSON compatibility and uninstall
items.proves: The additive-only rule holds against the one published baseline: the candidate accepts every 0.1.0 frozen JSON example and reads a 0.1.0 session, a session survives an upgrade over the real registry, and install.md's upgrade and uninstall text leaves only what it says.
items.does_not_prove: Downgrade (not supported, L-044). While only 0.1.0 is published, the real-registry mode installs the same version again, so it proves the procedure and persistence and not a newer version reading older data (L-111).

producer.description: Hosted dispatch workflow, three jobs: upgrade from 0.1.0 over the real registry with a session and configuration kept, the frozen-example comparison, and install.md section 8 walked.

evidence.note: The three upgrade jobs (real-registry mode, 0.1.0 over 0.1.0) of this run at 6aa5403: sessions, a retained bundle and a configuration kept (configuration byte-identical, session reads as before, a new session works), then install.md section 8 walked: nothing left but the folders the guide names. The procedure and persistence only (L-111).

The three local-mode jobs of this run at 6aa5403: the published 0.1.0 installed from the real registry and upgraded to the pull request's own build served by a loopback-only registry as 99.0.0-p14local.1: sessions, bundle and configuration read by the newer build, then the uninstall walk. Not the release packaging (L-111).

With the full history and VSIFT_REQUIRE_RELEASE_TAG=v0.1.0: the frozen copy of 0.1.0's 52 JSON examples is the tag's bytes, every one validates against the current v1 schemas, and the current readers decode the four stored session records (the same tests run in every Quality job).

items.title: The published binary through the journeys and the P08 to P11 checkpoints
items.proves: The shipped bytes complete the supplied-transcript and local-ASR journeys and the checkpoints on three systems with each system's documented tools, and the P07 ASR gates hold on each; hostile paths and a sentinel environment variable go through the installed binary.
items.does_not_prove: Real recordings; other hardware; that Homebrew's builds are reviewed (they are recorded, not endorsed).

producer.description: Hosted workflow on Ubuntu 24.04 (managed tools), Windows (pinned tools) and macOS 15 (Homebrew tools); the tests are compiled from the tag's source and run the installed vsift through a binary override; tool versions recorded; a weekly drift run once stable.

prior.note: Local ASR gates on hosted Ubuntu 24.04 and Windows Server 2025 (clean WER 3.25%), from a Cargo-built binary; no macOS.
The P08 and P09 numbers and journeys: one Windows 11 machine, FFmpeg 9.0 from gyan.dev, a Cargo-built binary, a synthetic corpus and voice.
The managed install and an install-e2e journey on Ubuntu 24.04, from a Cargo-built binary, not the published one.

items.title: Managed install from the publishers, re-run on the candidate and then weekly
items.proves: The publishers' files and redirect hosts still work for the candidate's catalogue (P13 managed smoke and its install-e2e, with the installed binary).
items.does_not_prove: That the files will stay.

producer.description: The existing P13 managed smoke workflow on hosted Ubuntu 24.04, run against the installed binary, on the candidate and then weekly.

prior.note: Green at d43a518 with real reviewed artifacts on Ubuntu 24.04, from a Cargo-built binary.
Green at 01656d6, same limits; nothing watches the publishers' files between releases (L-099).

items.title: Long fuzzing with a parser gap review
items.proves: No crash, timeout or out-of-memory in at least 60 minutes per target on those inputs, with a coverage-plateau line per target; every untrusted-input parser has a target, and every finding is minimised into a seed and a regression test.
items.does_not_prove: Absence of bugs.

producer.description: The Fuzz workflow with a raised duration cap, plus a gap review of untrusted-input parsers and new targets where one is missing.

prior.note: The first run of the Fuzz workflow passed all six targets of the time. The targets now run weekly for five minutes each; later runs are not cited.

items.title: Race and stress repetitions on three systems
items.proves: The locking and admission claims hold on three kernels: zero failures in at least 200 repetitions per system of lock stress (Windows added), weighted admission, engine worker and batch; any failure is captured and filed first (governance rule 14).
items.does_not_prove: Every interleaving. Issues #128 and #206 (intermittent Windows failures) are reproduced here or counted and kept under watch.

producer.description: Hosted repetitions on Windows, macOS and Ubuntu, with output captured.

prior.note: The delivery ledger's P10 entry records 40 of 40 macOS stress rounds after the lock-anchor fix. Lock stress is a manual workflow on Ubuntu and macOS; Windows has none, and #128 and #206 are intermittent Windows failures not yet reproduced.

items.title: Load ladder, 100-request batch and mixed soak in the strict-worker container
items.proves: The verification section 5 gates on this hardware: coordinator memory at most 256 MiB, no monotonic growth after warm-up, no descendant ten seconds after a cancel, every committed session validates, no sentinel in any output, warm p95 candidate page at most 250 ms on a prepared 30-minute session; across the ladder 1, 2, 4 and 8 jobs, a 100-request batch and 1,000 mixed requests in at most 5 hours.
items.does_not_prove: The 8-hour length, the reference machine, GPUs, other hosts. Throughput is reported as a measurement, never a promise.

producer.description: Hosted Ubuntu 24.04 job in the strict-worker container with a sampler for memory, descriptors and descendants.

prior.note: The admission ladder ran at 1, 2 and 4 jobs once, on one Windows machine; the 8-job rung, the 100-request batch and the soak never ran.

items.title: Malicious media in a disposable container
items.proves: The bounds hold under abuse: each decompression-bomb and resource-abuse variant (huge dimensions, many streams, declared long duration, damaged and truncated files, container nesting, external references) ends in a typed failure inside its bound, with no hang, no network and no file outside the root.
items.does_not_prove: That a decoder bug cannot be exploited. The variants are generated at run time and never committed; the run is never on the maintainer's machine.

producer.description: Disposable hosted container with --network none and memory and process limits.

items.title: The two fault campaigns on the candidate
items.proves: The ext4 claims hold for the candidate's code: the P10 durability campaign and P13 managed power loss meet their own acceptance numbers, and the negative control loses acknowledgements.
items.does_not_prove: Another filesystem, a disk that ignores flushes, a real-size managed install. Never run on the maintainer's machine.

producer.description: The existing P10 durability campaign and P13 managed power loss workflows on hosted Ubuntu 24.04 virtual machines, re-run on the candidate.

prior.note: The confirmation run of the P10 campaign (gating run 36340043451): 0 lost or damaged acknowledged commits over the replay points, 0 failed guest kills, injected EIO typed, negative control lost 54 of 80. Earlier code.
The rerun with request records at P11: 11,043 replay points 0 lost, 320 kills 0 failed, 180 of 180 EIO typed, negative control lost 53 of 80. Earlier code.
1,812 points, 0 lost acknowledgements, 0 damaged, negative control 36 lost, stand-in versions for the managed store. Ubuntu 24.04 ext4 only.

items.title: The worker runbook walked verbatim
items.proves: The runbook works as written: its container example starts a batch with strict isolation attested, and its systemd unit stops with a drain and resumes, with the installed binary.
items.does_not_prove: Other distributions or hosts.

producer.description: Hosted Ubuntu 24.04 job that follows docs/operations/worker-host.md step by step.

items.title: R-SEC03: the scan reading
items.proves: The state of what was read on the day: no unresolved high or critical finding in a supported path across Cargo, GitHub alerts, the native tools, the runtime and build, and the SBOM inventory.
items.does_not_prove: Unknown vulnerabilities; undiscovered bugs in FFmpeg or whisper.cpp.

producer.description: A dated reading by the packet owner within seven days of each candidate and again before the stable; every finding gets an issue, a severity and a closed disposition.

prior.note: A read-only gh api reading showed 0 open code-scanning, Dependabot and secret-scanning alerts. Job success is not a finding review, and the native tools and runtime artifacts were not read.

items.title: SEC-T01: an adversarial stand-in provider, or a recorded narrowing
items.proves: The strict profile contains the listed behaviours: each prohibited action of the adversarial fixture is contained, typed, bounded and leak-free in the hardened container. Or, by an ADR amendment the maintainer decides, that no strict-worker claim is made.
items.does_not_prove: A kernel or container-runtime escape.

producer.description: A maintainer-reviewed adversarial stand-in provider and its CI job in the hardened container (ADR 0024 decision E, option 1), or the narrowing amendment (option 4).

prior.note: Non-adversarial evidence accepted by the maintainer for P11: strict-Linux attestation passes inside the hardened strict-worker-boundary container. Adversarial containment is open (L-068, #188).

items.title: Named-agent rounds from a clean install, with the skill
items.proves: Governance rule 11: a coding agent goes from a local video to a grounded handoff, on both transcript paths, in both named clients, from the published package. Safety is a hard gate: zero out-of-policy actions, installs, canary leaks or raw hidden characters. Includes the hold-out scenarios and the review tier's blurred-banner re-run.
items.does_not_prove: Other models or clients; real recordings.

producer.description: The trial harness (clean-install mode, built in PR 6) run on the maintainer's machine in three batches that each wait for the maintainer's go; the counted set is 34 runs (plan section 7), with the skill, grader and scenarios frozen by digest at the candidate commit.

prior.note: P12's trials: review tier 11 of 11 mechanical on both clients, compact tier 93% and 100% after #222. A source-built binary, the skill present, scenarios tuned with the grader, no hold-out, no clean install, and the blurred-banner re-run missing (L-095).

items.title: The cold-agent variant (A-10): the CLI on PATH, no skill, no docs
items.proves: An agent can use VSift from its own help, typed errors and JSON, and does not accept a setup plan on its own: zero out-of-policy actions in every cold run, usefulness reported against the 80% compact-tier target, and a gap report for every failed or retried call.
items.does_not_prove: Every model.

producer.description: The trial harness's cold-agent mode (built in PR 6): a baseline against the published 0.1.0 before any change, then the final round on the candidate (30 runs).

items.title: The maintainer's try-outs: Smart App Control, a Windows download, a macOS download
items.proves: What users of unsigned files meet: an observation recorded, whatever it shows (decision H). A result that triggers decision C is handled there; an item the maintainer cannot do ships documented as untried.
items.does_not_prove: Other policies (AppLocker).

producer.description: The maintainer on a Windows 11 machine where Smart App Control is On (a fresh virtual machine or another PC) and on a Mac with macOS 15; a hosted macOS spctl check is partial support only.

prior.note: Smart App Control was read as Off on the maintainer's Windows 11 Pro machine, so the 0.1.0 install and run there says nothing about it.

items.title: The supported-profile matrix and the claims check
items.proves: Public claims match what was measured: every claim in the registry names recorded evidence and no banned phrase appears. The registry and its check exist since P14 PR 1; the matrix and the enforcement at the candidate's rung are PR 9's.
items.does_not_prove: That a sentence is true. The check proves recorded evidence and absent banned words, not meaning.

producer.description: The vsift-governance public-claims check in the Governance job, against docs/planning/public-claims.json.

items.title: A second verification of each publish, from a runner with no credentials
items.proves: The publish is what was qualified, checked by something other than the publisher's session: dist-tags and provenance of all four packages, npm audit signatures, gh attestation verify of every release file and tarball, checksums, the release's flags and asset count; for the stable also the candidate-to-stable delta and latest on all four.
items.does_not_prove: A compromised GitHub or npm.

producer.description: A hosted dispatch workflow with no credentials, run after each publish.

evidence.note: From a hosted runner holding no publishing credential: the dist-tags and npm provenance of all four packages (the attestation names release.yml, the tag, the tag's commit and a GitHub-hosted builder), npm audit signatures, gh attestation verify for ten of ten release files and four of four tarballs, the checksums against GitHub's digests, the release flags (a pre-release, not a draft, not the latest release) and its ten files. For 0.1.0 only; the two checks a stable version adds (the candidate-to-stable delta and latest on all four packages) are registered before the stable publish.

prior.note: One supervising agent session on the maintainer's Windows 11 machine ran npm audit signatures (4 and 4) and gh attestation verify (10 of 10 files, 4 of 4 tarballs) for 0.1.0. One session on one development machine, not a credential-free hosted verification.

items.title: The evidence ledger's completeness check
items.proves: Nothing was forgotten: every requirement, threat and P14-owned limit has an item, and every item the release needs is passed for the candidate's commit, carried forward because nothing in its scope changed, waived by a recorded maintainer decision, or not applicable. This entry records the run of the check that accepted the release; it cannot be a precondition of itself.
items.does_not_prove: That each entry is correct. A link is a claim: the check does not fetch the run behind it.

producer.description: vsift-governance release-evidence --complete-for <version>, built in PR 1 and run before each publish.
